fields.summary: TC-669-02: RRO Flag False When Duty Period Release Delay Equals Threshold (Boundary)

content.text: Linked Story: CREWCMBR-669
Precondition: A trip exists with a Duty Period where the actual release datetime is exactly at the RRO threshold (not greater than). Out of Scope: LCO, LRO, Guarantees, Special Rules.
TEST STEPS
Step
Action
Test Data
Expected Result
Set up a trip with a Duty Period where actualReleaseDateTimeUTC is exactly at the RRO threshold (equal to plannedRelease + threshold, not greater)
DP1: plannedRelease = 2026-03-03T22:00:00Z, actualRelease = 2026-03-04T00:00:00Z (exactly 120 min)
Trip payload is ready with DP release datetimes showing exactly 120 min delay (at boundary, not exceeding)
Trigger the RRO Lambda to process the Duty Period
DP with exactly 120 min release delay (boundary value)
Lambda is invoked successfully without errors
Calculate the difference between actualReleaseDateTimeUTC and plannedReleaseDateTimeUTC
actual - planned = 120 minutes exactly (equal to threshold, NOT greater than)
Difference calculated as 120 min - equal to threshold, RRO not triggered
Verify the rroEligible flag in the lambda output for the Duty Period
Delay = 120 min = threshold (not greater than), RRO not triggered
rroEligible = false
Confirm the DB update lambda persists rroEligible = false for the DP in DynamoDB
Lambda output payload with rroEligible=false
DynamoDB record shows rroEligible = false on the Duty Period
